To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) coupling to itinerant bosonic baths leads to delocalisation of a particle in a one-dimensional random potential, while coupling to localized bosonic baths leads the particle to remain localized; (ii) the delocalisation is due to the sub-diffusion (diffusion) of bosons; and (iii) delocalization occurs despite the fact that the frequency of the bosons is orders of magnitude smaller than that of the random potential.
(i) the particle remains localized when coupled to localized bosonic modes; (ii) the particle becomes delocalized when coupled to itinerant bosonic modes.
(a) coupling to bosons delocalizes the particle, and that (b) the delocalizing effect depends on the dynamics of bosons and not on the strength of the boson-particle interaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of the Anderson insulator when it is coupled to bosons of various types.

the dynamics of a particle in a random potential coupled to a bath of itinerant (hard core) bosons, which is a generic model of a quantum particle in a random environment interacting with phonons or magnons, respectively.
the dynamics of the Anderson insulator when it is coupled to a variety of bosonic baths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coupling the particle to a boson bath leads to delocalisation of the particle.
coupling of a particle in a one dimensional random potential to itinerant boson leads to delocalisation of the particle.

itinerancy of the bosons is the essential ingredient for delocalization of a particle in the Anderson insulator, and this result is valid for any kind of itinerant bath, be it phonons, bosons with a hard-core interaction or generic boson-bose interactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coupling of the particle to bosonic bath is sufficient to induce delocalization, while coupling of the particle with fermionic bath is not.
the dynamics of the Anderson insulator depends on the itineracy or the localization of the bosons.
the particle dynamics is dictated by the itinerancy of the bath and that itinerant boson bath can lead to delocalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of the system is determined by the nature of the boson bath, which is a result of the interplay between the particle-boson coupling and the boson-bosons interaction.
it is the bosonic itinerancy which is the essential ingredient for delocalization of a particle in random potential.
itineracy is a key ingredient for delocalization of a particle.
